last_material_result: One bounded distribution-gap validation tested the narrowed Seoul Venue Encore Cutoff Pages across Gocheok Sky Dome, KSPO DOME and Jamsil Indoor Gymnasium query clusters around 막차/귀가/앵콜. The pain itself is real: BiBibus explicitly sells concert return transport on the promise that fans can stay through the encore without last-train anxiety, and a past KSPO concert generated mainstream coverage framed around missing the last train. However, venue/event search results are dominated by broad ticket, seat-view, parking, food and access guides; direct event-title + 막차/귀가 intent did not surface as a stable discoverable cluster. The computed-cutoff answer remains differentiated, but distribution would require creating and maintaining event-specific pages before evidence of query demand exists. That maintenance-to-acquisition profile fails Lane A's low-maintenance portfolio bar. The active candidate is therefore KILLED rather than built.
economics: KRW0 spent. Direct payment was unlikely; monetization depended on ads, shuttle/taxi/lodging affiliate and event-title SEO. With fragmented observable search intent and per-event schedule/end-time maintenance required, expected contribution is too uncertain relative to maintenance burden. No build cost should be incurred.
next_checkpoint: Fresh DISCOVER on the next run. Prefer local/everyday utilities whose demand maps to stable recurring queries or durable public-data lookups rather than event-by-event content maintenance.
recommendation: KILL Seoul Venue Encore Cutoff Pages. Preserve the underlying insight—consumers pay to avoid last-train anxiety—but require a future recombination with stable distribution and lower content freshness burden before reconsidering it.
